newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-SAQLAIN SPINS PAKISTAN TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SAQLAIN SPINS PAKISTAN TO VICTORY.

text.p: Pakistan spinner Saqlain Mushtaq claimed five wickets to inspire his side to a narrow 12-run victory over Australia in the limited-overs World Series competition on Sunday.
Saqlain produced two outstanding spells of accurate off-spin bowling to finish with figures of five for 29 in 8.5 overs in Pakistan's opening match in the triangular tournament.
Chasing Pakistan's total of 223 all out in 49.5 overs, Australia were dismissed for 211 in 47.5 overs after Saqlain took the last two wickets in successive deliveries.
But his most telling contribution came in the 46th over when he removed all-rounders Steve Waugh for 57 and Tom Moody for eight.
His other victims were opener and captain Mark Taylor, wicketkeeper Ian Healy and leg-spinner Shane Warne.
It was Australia's first taste of defeat at home this season following victories in the first two tests against West Indies and the opening two World Series matches against the same opponents.
Pakistan, who arrived in Australia last Wednesday, will face the West Indies in Adelaide in their next World Series match on Tuesday.
After conceding a miserly 16 runs from his opening seven overs, Saqlain wrestled the initiative from Australia when Waugh looked poised to guide the home side to safety.
Saqlain combined with leg-spinner Mushtaq Ahmed to pin down the Australian batsmen during the middle stages of Australia's innings, gradually increasing the pressure on the opposition.
Earlier, Pakistan opener Aamir Sohail scored a patient 67, including six fours and one six, to lay the foundation of his side's total.
Sohail added 102 runs for the second wicket with number three Mohammad Wasim, who contributed 44 before Pakistan lost their last five wickets for 32 in pursuit of quick runs.
